description:
FILED s536i (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) while fixing #4682 (scratch/s536i/p/e1.pl, f1.pl in the s536i worktree).  PRE-EXISTING: main 0ac58419 answers the same.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3):

    my @b = (1,2,3); my $s = \((@b)[7]); print scalar(@b), "\n";      # perl 3, PCL 8
    my $t = \((@b, 1)[9]); print scalar(@b), "\n";                     # the literal-list spelling

MECHANISM (read): `\TERM` generates the term in lvalue context (ExprToCL::_backslash_lvalue_form), so a list slice lowers to `(p-backslash (p-aref-deref-box @b 7))`, and p-aref-deref-box's scalar-index arm is `(p-aref-box (p-ensure-arrayref ref) idx)` -- the EAGER element accessor, which extends the array.  s536i (#4682) gave the OTHER aliasing consumers (foreach / map / grep / a user-sub argument) the list slice's own cells through %p-aliasing-slice-form -> %p-lslice-aliases (a missing element there is a lazy alias over the list and creates nothing); `\` is not one of that rule's consumers.  Fix shape: `\` of a LIST SLICE (ExprToCL::_is_list_slice_node) refers to %p-lslice-aliases' cells (p-refgen-list over them, or the one cell for a single index) instead of the eager -box head.  Perl also dies on a WRITE through such a ref only when the list held a literal; an in-range array element stays the element (`\((@b)[1])` writes $b[1] -- correct today, keep it).
subject: SILENT WRONG: `\((@b)[7])` -- a reference to a list slice's element PAST THE END -- grows @b to 8 (perl leaves @b alone: a list slice reads, it never extends its source)
